Posted January 30, 2004
Analysis by Richard Cowan
See
UK Reefer Madness Spreads To Canada As Both Countries Move Toward Phoney Decrim Bills. One Cannabis User Dies of An Overdose, Another Commits Murder.

This has been an extraordinary week in the UK.

On Tuesday, the Blair government, which has a 161-seat majority in the House of Commons, avoided a ruinous defeat by only five votes on a bill that will raise tuition for some students at Britain's underfunded universities.

Amazingly, the amount of money involved was only about 2 billion dollars. (Estimates on the direct costs of cannabis prohibition in the UK start at over $500 million, and much more is lost in taxes.) While Blair won, he was badly damaged by the battle.

Then on Wednesday, Blair dodged another bullet when a judge ruled that he had not lied about an intelligence report on Iraq's WMDs, and that the BBC had falsely accused him of doing so. (A majority of the people seem to think that the report was a whitewash, but heads rolled at the BBC.)

As the final act in this week's circus, the UK's new cannabis laws went into force yesterday after weeks of reefer madness and endless blather even in the better papers and on the BBC, but no judge will object.

When the subject is cannabis, most of the British political class seems indifferent to facts and impervious to reason.
See
Embarrassing Questions: If It Was Wrong to Lie to Justify the War on Saddam, Why Isn't It Wrong to Lie to Justify the War on Cannabis Users? Analysis by Richard Cowan

More than two years in the making, this mess ultimately pleased no one. It is not real decriminalization, inasmuch as the police will still have the option of arresting anyone for possession, if they want to. (The penalties for growing and selling remain the same.)

In fact, all that happened was that cannabis was reclassified from Class B meth and barbiturates to Class C (valium and other benzodiazepine tranquilizers and steroids.)
See
UK Committee Will Endorse Reclassification Decriminalization By Another Name, But Says Real Decriminalization Would Send the Wrong Message Cannabis Equals Valium Is The Right Message?
and
The Lancet Reports That Thousands Are Killed In Accidents Caused By Tranquilizers
and
UK Victims of Tranquilizers Urge That " Far Safer " Medical Cannabis Be Made Available IoS " More people died from benzodiazepine usage than from such drugs as heroin and cocaine. "

Nonetheless, the prohibitionist reacted with hysteria.

Melanie Phillips, who got too crazy even for Rupert Murdoch's London Times, (SeeLondon Sunday Times Contribution to the Cannabis Debate Is Just More Reefer Madness) wrote a column in the Daily Mail, in which she claims, The UN's International Narcotics Control Board has warned of worldwide repercussions from the British initiative, which other countries fear will undermine their own anti-drug campaigns and encourage cannabis cultivation.
See
UN Nark's Speech To Swedish Prohibitionists May Cause Permanent Brain Damage. Illogic, Ignorance and Lying, Especially About the Dutch, Of Course.
and
Is The UN An Instrument of Peace and Freedom Or Of War and Tyranny? UN Narks Make Answer Clear. Lies and Hatred In Service To International Police State. (International Narcotics Control Board Report)
and
The UN Commission on Narcotic Drugs Resolution on the Control of Cannabis in Africa. UN Narks Urge War on Poorest of the Poor. Cannabis Prohibition Does Most Damage In Poor Countries.
and links

If such an international misunderstanding seems improbable, it is nothing compared with the purported confusion among Britons.

The police and their prohibitionist flacks have been saying that children of all ages (and under the nanny state everyone is a child) somehow think that reclassification means legalization and comparable to Valium means harmless and suitable for use in elementary schools.

This same claim was made following the Brixton experiment in which the police stopped arresting adults for possession in one London area known for its hard drug problems.
See
If The Best Two Word Explanation for Cannabis Prohibition Is Bad Journalism, The Best 3 Word Explanation Is Quack, Quack, Quack. -- Wholesale Malpractice In UK As Lambeth Experiment Spreads.

Of course, no one has cited any actual survey that shows that anyone really thinks any such thing, but the Blair government quickly blew a million pounds (US$1.85 million) on an advertising campaign to explain the obvious.

The left of center anti-prohibitionist Guardian even ran an article, Cannabis not risk free, says adviser, which reported, The government adviser who recommended today's downgrading of cannabis in the hierarchy of dangerous illegal drugs has repeated his warning that it is still harmful to health.
See
Marijuana Isn't Harmless. Okay, But Why Isn't It Sold Over the Counter? Or Would You Ban Something That Causes 300,000 ER Visits Every Year, And Kills A Child Every Month? (Trick Question)

Actually, it was a good article, and beyond the usual warnings about possible dangers, the real news was something else:
In an interview with the Guardian earlier this week Sir Michael (Rawlins) revealed that the ACMD (Advisory Council on the Misuse of Drugs) was reviewing the classification system, which grades drugs by degree of harm into A, B and C.

Members want a more " objective " system to avoid inappropriate penalties or police powers.

Obviously, that is something that desperately needs to be done. The UK government web site explains the purpose of their classification system:

Why are drugs classified A, B or C?

The Misuse of Drugs Act 1971 places drugs into one of three categories, A, B or C, for the purposes of control. Classification broadly reflects the risks and harms caused by misuse of the controlled drug in question, and is reflected in penalty levels for drugs offences.

Reclassification sends a more credible message to young people that all drugs are harmful, but some are more harmful than others.

It would be difficult to pick one news article (as opposed to opinion pieces) as the worst of the bunch, but the winner might be Cannabis Causes 'Considerable Harm', Say Gps fromThe Scotsmanof Edinburgh.

It was written by John von Radowitz, who is actually called the Science Correspondent for the UK Press Association.
January 27, 2004

GPs today joined doctors leaders and other experts warning about the dangers of cannabis.

The Royal College of General Practitioners called for a debate on the health risks of the drug, due to be downgraded from class B to class C on Thursday.

It said cannabis could do considerable harm and should not be regarded as safe.

RCGP spokeswoman Dr Clare Gerada said: The evidence that it produces dependence is beyond dispute, with around 5% to 10% eventually becoming dependent.
(MarijuanaNews note: Dr Gerada was quoted in If The Best Two Word Explanation for Cannabis Prohibition Is Bad Journalism, The Best 3 Word Explanation Is Quack, Quack, Quack. -- Wholesale Malpractice In UK As Lambeth Experiment Spreads. )

Cannabis also impairs concentration, short-term memory, attention and rational thought, driving and piloting skills and amplifies the driving impairments caused by simultaneous alcohol use.

Larger amounts of cannabis can produce anxiety and depression, psychotic states lasting several days and an increased risk of developing schizophrenia.

She said the college had no view on the rights and wrongs of legislation but the dangers of cannabis needed to be explored.

Cannabis contains more than 400 chemicals, she said, including about 60 known cancer triggers, and was stronger today than it was 20 or 30 years ago.

Genetically modified cannabis had concentrated the active ingredients in the drug.
(MarijuanaNews note: Of course, cannabis has not been genetically modified. However, that scares people, so it is better than just saying that it has been bred.)

A joint in the 1980s contained about 10mg of THC, the main active chemical, compared with up to 300mg today.
(MarijuanaNews note: This is an excellent example of pseudo-science, by an incompetent science correspondent. Instead of just saying that cannabis potency has increased 30 fold in just 20 years, he says it has gone from about 10mg of THC compared with up to 300mg today. One would assume that this is for a one gram joint, but again it's the scare that counts.

In fact, there is absolutely no data to support such claims about increased cannabis potency in the UK. The prohibitionists have successfully imported the DEAland party line, and no one ever asks to see the supporting data.

The Daily Telegraph even published a piece called,Cannabis factfilewhich claimed, THC (the hallucinogenic component of cannabis) content ranges from eight per cent to 20 per cent in today's spliffs, much more potent than pot smoked in the 1960s and 1970s.
See
Dan Forbes Documents Walters Lies About Potency. Understanding That The War On Cannabis Is Built On Lies Is Key to Understanding More Than Just Drug War.

Moreover, twenty years ago, virtually all of the cannabis consumed in the UK was hashish, cannabis resin, but today more than half of the cannabis consumed there is homegrown, and hash has become ever more diluted by all sorts of harmful substances.

In 1983, the average potency of contraband cannabis sampled by the US government was around 3% THC. Today, it appears to be a little less than 6%.)

The RCGP pointed out that since GPs dealt with patients affected by cannabis, they were well placed to offer information and advice.
(MarijuanaNews note: We can see what experts their spokesquacks are, but they could never judge relative risks if they do not know how many of their patients use cannabis without problems.)

The British Medical Association has already said it is extremely concerned that the imminent downgrading of cannabis would send the wrong message to the public.

Ranking cannabis as a class C drug put it alongside bodybuilding steroids and some anti-depressants.
(MarijuanaNews note: No, not anti-depressants (which are serotonin uptake inhibitors like Prozac), but tranquilizers. Science Correspondent indeed! But even if he had been correct about the anti-depressants, it would be a dubious parallel, at best.)
See
Indianapolis Star Reports: " Eli Lilly Doing Spin Control After News Oregon Shooter Took Prozac "
and
DEAland Children Consume 90% of the World's Ritalin. " This year six million children across the USA -- over one tenth of the schoolage population -- will be prescribed anti-depressants and stimulants. " Context for The Medical Marijuana Debate and " Drug Education "

And medical science is clearly in a perilous condition when Peter Maguire, the deputy chairman of the British Medical Association's board of science can be quoted in the Telegraph as saying, People are making the conclusion that it is safe where in fact it is actually more dangerous than tobacco. "
See
British Lung Foundation Cons Media. Blaming Cannabis for Problems Caused By Prohibition. Tripping Over the Party Line. The Media Fell For It, As Usual, But UK Anti-Tobacco Group Does Not.

He is quoted in the Times as saying that he wanted the Government to keep the decision under constant review and to be prepared to reclassify cannabis as a class B drug.

That would put it back with barbiturates.

Here is what Drugs.com says about barbiturates: withdrawal side effects (for example, anxiety or restlessness, convulsions [seizures], feeling faint, nausea or vomiting, trembling of hands, trouble in sleeping) occurring after the medicine is stopped

If you think you or someone else may have taken an overdose of this medicine, get emergency help at once . Taking an overdose of a barbiturate or taking alcohol or other CNS depressants with the barbiturate may lead to unconsciousness and possibly death. Some signs of an overdose are severe drowsiness, severe confusion, severe weakness, shortness of breath or slow or troubled breathing, slurred speech, staggering, and slow heartbeat.

Would Maguire say that there are comparable risks in taking cannabis?

Or would he say that the risks in taking cannabis are greater than in taking benzodiazepines?

Consider this:
It is a well-established fact that long-term benzodiazepine use leads to physical and mental health problems. In addition there were 1810 deaths from benzodiazepine overdose 1990-1996 according to Home Office Statistics and there are an estimated 1600 benzodiazepine-related traffic accidents with 110 deaths each year in the UK.

That description comes from http://www.benzo.org.uk/ashdoh.htm. Ironically, it was written by Dame Heather Ashton, one of the leading proponents of reefer madness and cannabis prohibition in the UK. (Try doing a search under Ashton on MarijuanaNews.)

Can science or just common sense prevail over quacks and hacks? Is fact checking only for foreign wars?

Perhaps the greatest irony this week came from a poll showing that the British people actually favor either real decriminalization (28%) or outright legalization (23%). In other words, 51% believe that marijuana should be either decriminalized or legalized, but they do not think that it is harmless because unlike the quacks and hacks, they know that in the real world nothing is completely harmless for everyone under all circumstances, and they know that harmlessness is not a prerequisite for legalization or nothing would be legal.

Thus the politicians are running away from the people, especially the younger generation. Under 35, almost two thirds want cannabis either decriminalised (32%) or completely legalised (31%). But among people over 65, only one-third favour either of these options; 61% think the sale and possession of soft drugs should remain a criminal offence.
From http://www.yougov.com/yougov_website/asp_besPollArchives/bes_kelMain.asp?aId=951&sID=2&wID=0&UID=

The majority of respondents thought of cannabis as less addictive than legal drugs like coffee, alcohol, and cigarettes. If a cannabis user also used hard drugs, the vast majority of respondents (83%) felt that it was not a result of cannabis creating a craving for harder drugs, but that they did so because cannabis users find themselves part of a drug culture with dealers pushing both hard and soft drugs.
See
The Gateway Theory Won't Die Because It Tells Prohibitionists Something They Want to Believe, But The Truth Tells Them Something They Refuse to Hear.

The YouGov Poll included more than 2,500 participants. They were certainly better informed than the quacks and Science Correspondents.

Finally, two quick items to top-off the absurdity.

A few months ago, Prime Minister Blair was rushed to the hospital suffering from a heart condition that was blamed on strong coffee he drank in France, and subsequently it was announced that he was quitting coffee.

Yesterday, the police in Edinburgh arrested three people at Scotland's first coffee shop, but not for possession of coffee.
